paperTitle: CancerSP: A Serious Game for Prostate Cancer Decision-Making and Planning Skills
centralContribution: This work introduces CancerSP, a prototype serious game designed to enhance decision-making and planning skills for medical professionals and students in the context of prostate cancer. The game replicates classic real-world prostate symptoms, treatment patterns, and care pathways, challenging players to concurrently manage multiple patients and make critical decisions to prevent patient fatalities.

units.title: Central Contribution
units.summary: CancerSP: serious game for prostate cancer decision-making skills.

content.description: CancerSP is a serious game prototype designed to improve decision-making and planning skills for medical professionals and students in prostate cancer. It simulates real-world symptoms and treatment pathways, requiring players to manage multiple patients simultaneously and make critical decisions to prevent fatalities. This work addresses a critical gap in interactive educational tools, offering a risk-free environment for complex clinical prioritization, moving beyond simple awareness to comprehensive training in patient care.

units.whyThisUnit: This unit directly presents the core innovation and purpose of the paper, serving as the central contribution.

units.title: Abstract
units.summary: Overview of prostate cancer education challenges and CancerSP's solution.

content.description: Prostate cancer, a globally common and fatal disease, necessitates early diagnosis and effective management. While computer games can facilitate healthcare learning, there's a gap in interactive tools for prostate cancer decision-making and planning, especially for multi-patient management. Existing apps mainly focus on awareness, not complex clinical prioritization in a risk-free environment. CancerSP fills this void, offering a dynamic platform for medical professionals and students to hone critical skills.
